content.title: About
content.content: Honeycrisp is a apple variety known for its crisp texture, sweet‑tart flavor, and bright red skin. The apples are eaten raw, preserving all nutrients and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The variety was developed in the United States in the 1970s and quickly gained popularity for its taste and storage qualities.
Honeycrisp apples stay crunchy even after several weeks of refrigeration.
The skin holds most of the antioxidants, so it’s best to keep it on.
The variety is frequently used in baking, salads, and juices because it holds up well to heat.
Honeycrisp is considered one of the sweetest apple varieties while retaining a pleasant acidity.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Apples provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols in the skin protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: An apple is a light snack, containing about 52 kcal per 100 g.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium in apples helps maintain healthy blood pressure.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to apples, especially if they are sensitized to pollen.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic apples, wash them thoroughly to remove possible chemical residues.

items.title: Digestive issues
items.content: A high intake of fiber can cause discomfort for people with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Honeycrisp apples can be eaten whole, sliced into salads, juiced, made into sauces, or used in baking. Keeping the skin on retains the maximum amount of nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store apples in the refrigerator’s fruit drawer, in a perforated plastic bag. At room temperature they last 1‑2 days; in the fridge they keep for up to 4 weeks.
